implementation_notes: The standard library ships the pattern: require 'delegate' gives SimpleDelegator, which forwards every message the target responds to and allows swapping the target later via __setobj__, and Delegator as the abstract customization point; DelegateClass(superclass) generates a typed delegator. Ruby's dynamic dispatch also makes method_missing plus respond_to_missing? the hand-written form, and Forwardable provides explicit def_delegators forwarding when the delegated surface should be listed. Prefer the stdlib over hand-rolled method_missing - it already handles respond_to?, protected methods and BasicObject edge cases - and write an ordinary forwarding class when you need a named type with a stable, documented public API.
pitfalls: method_missing only sees calls the proxy does not define: a name that clashes with Kernel or Delegator methods silently bypasses the target, and respond_to?/respond_to_missing? must be kept in sync.
SimpleDelegator is a different class from the target - is_a?/instance_of? checks fail - and private methods are not forwarded.
Delegator inherits from BasicObject, so ordinary Object methods (to_s, inspect, !~) come from its own Kernel copy; identity and equality stay the proxy's, not the target's.
